findings: The preserved source asks only for linked-list nodes reversed in groups of K; it does not specify API shape, behavior for a final short group, allocation policy, invalid K or cyclic inputs.
The candidate makes the common complete-group-only contract explicit instead of attributing the short-tail rule to the source.

The pointer boundaries are coherent: groupPrev precedes the group, kth is the group end, groupNext is excluded from reversal, and prev starts at groupNext so the old group head reconnects to the suffix during reversal.
The implementation probes a full K-node group before mutating pointers, preventing partial reversal and rollback problems when the remaining suffix is too short.

The standalone Java implementation preserves original node identities, introduces no cycles and matches an independent array grouping reference across fixed cases and 3000 deterministic generated cases.
The candidate correctly treats k=1, empty input and k greater than list length as explicit boundaries and rejects k<1 under the answer-side contract.
No production linked-list topology or project experience is invented; cyclic-input semantics are explicitly left outside the finite-list contract.
